solution.content: Me and my friends We always put the second person before the first person in a positive sentence according to the order of pronouns. solution.content: the very well-directed film The ‘film’ mentioned in the given sentence is not specific and we generally use the indefinite article ‘a’ before a non-specific noun. Hence, ‘a very well directed’ is the most appropriate answer.

solution.content: this year it reflect badly The given sentence is a conditional sentence which has a futuristic sense so the verb used must be in the future tense(will). Hence, ‘it will reflect badly’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We stayed / in Jim’s flat / during he was / on holiday.

solution.content: during he was ‘When’ is used for talking about the time at which something happens or happened. The given sentence talks about the time at which Jim was on holiday. Hence, ‘when he was’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Do you / recall to meet / her at the party / last night?

solution.content: recall to meet The given sentence will have a bare infinitive (without the preposition ‘to’). Hence, ‘recall meeting’ is the most appropriate answer.

solution.content: having the trouble ‘Taking the trouble’ is grammatically the correct phrase for the given sentence. Hence, ‘having’ will be replaced with ‘taking’ & ‘taking the trouble’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This is / too grave sin / to be / pardoned.

solution.content: too grave sin We will put the indefinite article ‘a’ before ‘sin’ as the sin is not-specific. Hence, ‘too grave a sin’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The policeman asked / many people but / no one was knowing / how the accident happened.

solution.content: no one was knowing The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its past form(V 2 ) and not in the past continuous form(was +V-ing). Hence, ‘no one knew(V 2 )’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This question / is quite too / simple for me / to answer.

solution.content: is quite too The use of ‘quite’ is irrelevant in the grammatical context of the given sentence as ‘too…to’ is a fixed pair. Hence, ‘is too simple for me to answer’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: You should / have respond / to my query / sooner.

solution.content: have respond “Have + V 3 (third form of the verb)” is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘have responded( V 3 )’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The manager said, “Could you please confirm me whether you have received all the items that you had ordered?”

solution.content: confirm me whether you The use of the pronoun ‘me’ is grammatically incorrect in the given sentence so it must be removed. Hence, ‘confirm whether you’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We thought / there was a good idea / to wear snow boots / before we stepped out.

solution.content: there was a good idea ‘Idea’ in the given sentence is a singular subject and for it, we will use ‘it’ as a singular pronoun and not ‘there’. Hence, ‘it was a good idea’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: There have been /three breaks-in /in our society/ this month.

solution.content: three breaks-in ‘Break-in’ is a phrasal verb which means to enter a building by force, usually in order to steal something. However, the given sentence talks about three attempts so we will use the plural form of ‘break-in’. Hence, ‘three break-ins’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He / can have been / more polite / to her.

solution.content: No error.

question.content: Several minutes passed / before she returned / carry milk / for the dog.

question.content: The Taj Mahal / is one of / the most beautiful / creation in the world.

solution.content: creation in the world According to the “ Subject-Verb Agreement Rule ”, ‘ One of/ Each of/ Most of/ None of + Plural Subject” is grammatically the correct structure. Similarly, the given sentence will have ‘creations’ as a plural subject. Hence, ‘creations in the world’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This park is / the largest bird sanctuary / in the State.

solution.content: No error.

solution.content: No error.

question.content: We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market

solution.content: two dozens We never write ‘dozens’ if we are using a numerical amount like two, three, etc. before it. For example, ‘two dozens of bananas’ is incorrect but ‘three dozen of mangoes’ is correct. Similarly, the given sentence has ‘two’ as a numerical value. Hence, ‘two dozen’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.

solution.content: your work ‘Our’ is the possessive form of ‘we’ and it means something belonging to us(more than a single person). Similarly in the given sentence, the work belongs to both the persons and not to a single person. Hence, ‘our work’ is the most appropriate structure.

question.content: I do not / like to read / these kind / of novels.

solution.content: these kind ‘This’ and ‘kind’ are in singular form whereas ‘These’ and ‘kinds’ are in plural form. Hence,‘these kinds’ will be grammatically correct for the given sentence.

question.content: Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?

solution.content: for walking When we use verbs like walk, talk, ride, drink, etc. as nouns, we put the indefinite article ‘a’ before them as per their sound. For example, we had a talk, let's go for a drive, etc. Hence, ‘for a walk’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.

solution.content: Among you and me We use ‘among’ for more than two persons and ‘between’ for two persons. However, there are two persons mentioned in the given sentence. Hence, ‘Between you and me’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I find that / I get myself tired / very easily / these days.

solution.content: I get myself tired The use of the reflexive pronoun ‘myself’ is irrelevant according to the grammatical context of the sentence so it will be removed. Hence, ‘I get tired’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: If you have / remained calm / you could have / saved the situation.

solution.content: If you have If you have “ If + had + V 3 …. could have + V 3 ( third form of the verb )” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘If you had’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I will spend / my rest of remaining / life in my / native village.

solution.content: my rest of remaining We cannot use ‘rest’ & ‘remaining’ together in a sentence as it becomes the case of superfluousness(not necessary). Hence, ‘remaining’ will be removed from the sentence & ‘the rest of my life’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We yet / have time / to catch / the bus.

solution.content: We yet ‘Still’ means starting in the past and continuing until now. However, ‘still’ generally comes before a verb in the present perfect form(has/have) and ‘yet’ usually comes at the end of the sentence. Similarly in the given sentence, the time for catching the bus has started in the past and continued till now. Hence, ‘We still’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This dog seems / to be very ferocious, / otherwise, / it is harmless.

solution.content: Otherwise ‘Otherwise‘ is a conjunction that means apart from that. However, ‘But’ is also a conjunction that is used for introducing an idea that contrasts with or is different from what has just been said. Similarly in the given sentence, the statement that the dog is harmless contrasts with its characteristic of being ferocious(violent). Hence, ‘But’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The girl lay down / on the bed / besides her mother / and went to sleep.

solution.content: besides her mother ‘Besides’ means ‘in addition to something’ & ‘Beside’ means ‘at the side of, or next to somebody/something’. However, the given sentence states that the girl lay down on the bed next to her mother and went to sleep. Hence, ‘beside her mother’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He went / to the bed / with a / slight fever.

solution.content: to the bed We generally use the phrases ‘go to bed’, ‘gone to bed’ or ‘went to bed’. Hence, we will remove the definite article ‘the’ from the given sentence and ‘went to bed’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The city turned out / to be very / different to what / he had expected.

solution.content: different to what There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘to’ after ‘different’ must be replaced with ‘from’ because ‘different’ generally takes the preposition ‘from’ with it. Hence, ‘different from what’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Your name / precedes before / mine / in the list.

solution.content: precedes before We cannot write ‘precedes’ and ‘before’ together in a sentence as they have similar meanings & that will become a case of superfluousness (not necessary). Hence, ‘before’ must be removed from the sentence to make it grammatically correct.

question.content: You should / avail this opportunity / to demonstrate / your skills.

solution.content: avail this opportunity ‘Avail’ always takes the preposition ‘of’ and a reflexive pronoun(myself, yourself, ourselves, etc.) in accordance with the given subject(You). Hence, ‘avail yourself of this opportunity’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.

solution.content: he had been failed The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its simple past form(failed) and not in the past perfect form(had been failed). Hence, ‘he failed’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He often / persists to ask / awkward questions / at the board meetings.

solution.content: persists to ask “ Persist + in + V-ing ” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, the preposition ‘to’ must be replaced with the preposition ‘in’ and ‘persists in asking(V-ing)’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

question.content: His son-in-laws / have enhanced / his business / within a short period.

solution.content: His son-in-laws We can never write ‘in-laws’ because it is incorrect to add ‘s’ in the suffix(of law). However, we generally write son-in-law for a single male and sons-in-law for more than one male. Similarly, the given sentence talks about two males. Hence, ‘His sons-in-law’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A businessman / at our colony / was found / COVID positive.

solution.content: At our colony The preposition ‘at’ is used when you are at a specific address, at a general location, and at a point. However, the preposition ‘in’ is used in a space, neighborhood, city and country. Similarly, the given sentence talks about a businessman in the neighborhood(colony). Hence, ‘in our colony’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Either of these / two roads / lead to / the post office.

solution.content: lead to According to the “ Subject-Verb Agreement Rule ”, ‘ Either of/ Neither of + Plural Subject + Singular verb ’ is grammatically the correct structure. The given sentence has ‘Roads’ as a plural subject and ‘leads’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘leads to’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: His father / prevented him / to go abroad / for higher studies.

solution.content: to go abroad We generally use the preposition ‘from’ with prevent not ‘to’. Hence, we will replace ‘to’ with ‘from’ and ‘from going abroad’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

question.content: What is the name / of the Swami / whom autobiography / impressed you so much?

solution.content: whom autobiography 'Whom' is an object pronoun that refers to the person who was the recipient of an action. However, 'Whose' is a possessive pronoun that refers to the person to whom something belongs. Similarly, the given sentence refers to a Swami to whom the autobiography belongs. Hence, ‘whose autobiography’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The crowd of the migrant worker at the station for the Shramik Special is unforgettable.

question.content: Will you / listen me / when I tell you / the details?

solution.content: listen me There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘to’ is missing after ‘listen’. Hence, ‘listen to me’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The crow held back / to the piece / of bread / with its claws.

solution.content: The crow held back ‘Held back’ means to not do something & ‘held on’ means to maintain a grasp on something.Both are phrasal verbs. Similarly, in the given sentence, the crow grasps the piece of bread with its claws. Hence, ‘the crow held on’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The farmer is / cutting the corn / which has ripen / in the fields.

solution.content: which has ripen ‘Has + V 3 ’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. However, the V 3 form of ‘ripen’ is ‘ripened’. Hence, ‘has ripened’ is the most appropriate answer.

solution.content: we would met The form of the verb ‘meet’ is incorrect(met) in the context of the given sentence. It should be written in the simple present form(meet). Hence, ‘we would meet’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Obi wanted / to continue on / his idea of / building a modern school.

solution.content: to continue on There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. Use the preposition ‘on’ in place of ‘with’. Hence, ‘to continue with’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Since India has started doing well in hockey it had once again become a popular sport.

solution.content: it had once again The given sentence is in the present perfect tense so the verb must be used in the present perfect form and not in the past perfect form. Hence, ‘it has once again’ is the most appropriate answer.

solution.content: No error.

question.content: I was watching a whole scene very carefully.

question.content: Google has set on an India fund and announced an investment of ten billion dollars.

question.content: I was thrilled to going out with my friend for the film.

solution.content: to going out The structure ‘thrilled to + V 1 ’ is grammatically correct. Hence, ‘thrilled to go(V 1 ) out’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Rohit said that he would save me from been scold by father.

solution.content: been scold “being + V 3 (third form of the verb)” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘being scolded(V 3 )’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Mr. Choudhri goes to fly to Germany and France next weekend.

solution.content: Mr. Choudhri goes The given sentence talks about a future action(next weekend), . The structure ‘is going to’ is generally used for future actions. Hence, ‘Mr. Choudhri is going to’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.

solution.content: Not get The given sentence must start with a verb ‘do’ which is missing. Hence, ‘Do not get’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Mr. Roy was not only very successful and humble also.

solution.content: and humble also “Not only- But also” is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘but also humble’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The man we met was any other than the original owner of the house.

solution.content: was any other The phrase ‘any other’ will be replaced with ‘different’ which means not the same person. Hence, ‘was different than’ is the most appropriate answer.

solution.content: me always The word ‘always’ must be replaced with an adverb ‘anytime’ to grammatically correct the given sentence.

question.content: The man whose sitting at the corner table is my uncle.

question.content: Jagdeep, the Bollywood comedian, began his film career at eight as a live childlike actor in the 1950’s.

solution.content: as a live childlike actor The usage of the word live is incorrect. The word lively will be used here as an adjective. Lively means full of energy and excitement.

question.content: Hundred and fifty rupees seem a high price for this little vase.

solution.content: seem a high price The amount, Time, Distance, etc are considered as singular units and singular verbs are used for them. For example, that hundred rupee note is mine. I feel a six-hour-long journey is exhausting for me, etc. Similarly in the given sentence ‘Hundred and fifty rupees’ is a singular subject that will take ‘seems’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘seems a high price’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: There is no one else in this house; I can feel the presence.

solution.content: no one else If one can feel the presence, it is obvious that there is someone present. Hence, ‘no one’ will be replaced with ‘someone’ to make the given sentence grammatically correct.

question.content: You look very tired; you would go to bed now.

solution.content: you would go There is a modal verb error in the given sentence. The modal verb ‘would’ must be replaced with ‘should’ as the sentence is showing a sense of suggestion. Hence, ‘you should go’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The little baby cried loudly to a new toy.

solution.content: to a ‘Cry for something’ is a phrase that means to express a want or need through crying. Similarly in the given sentence, the child is expressing his need for the toy through crying. Hence, ‘for a toy’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: My sister prefers tea than coffee in the after lunch. (Morning)

question.content: This is the place here Sudhir found the wallet full of money.

question.content: Although we took all precautions but we were unable to avoid getting caught in the heavy rain.

question.content: I’m sure that I found the place without any difficulty when I go next time.

question.content: Asking for and giving informations is an important feature of conversations.

question.content: My father made me to do the French grammar exercise again and again.

question.content: They could be pass their exams if they studied harder.

solution.content: They could be The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its past form(would). Hence, ‘They would pass’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Every country tries to do its good at the Olympic games as they are held in great prestige.

solution.content: its good Replace “its good” by “well”. Good' is an adjective like a good boy, a good book, etc & 'Well' is an adverb like, He performed well. Similarly, in the given sentence, we need an adverb to modify the verb 'do'. Hence, 'well' is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Judy solved the difficult problem by her own without anyone’s help.

solution.content: by her own There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘by’ must be replaced with ‘on’. Hence, ‘on her own’ is the most appropriate structure. “On her own” means by herself and unaided.

question.content: You must avoid riding in a crowded bus / or travelling in a metro / during rush hour / as both are quiet unpleasant experiences.

as both are quiet unpleasant experiences

question.content: The river appears to have / got its name / from the town nearby.

question.content: A. When Franco was young; he would stay at sea all night. B. Every , he would arrive with a big catch of fresh fish and sell it in the market. C. Franco was a fisherman who lived on the beach. D. He had been fishing for as long as he could remember. (Evening)

question.content: S-1 When Amit woke up in the and looked at his face in the mirror, he did not recognise the face looking back at him. A: The face staring at him was calm and cool. question.content: S-1 Both the boys were without helmets and were bleeding profusely. A. The timely help saved the lives of the boys who were ashamed of their actions after meeting Mohan. B. question.content: A. First it is received by the sub-editors through the correspondents, the reporters, and via the news agencies. B. question.content: Our twelve years in the forest were  A.  Ram had lost, we would have to  B.  ending. Now, according to the wager  C.  discovered our whereabouts, we would have to endure  another ten years in exile  D.  spend a year in hiding. If during this year Mohan

question.content: Neither of the biscuits you gave me _________ chocolate chips.

solution.content: contains ‘Everyone/each/ every/ nothing/ everything/ anything/ either/ neither’ represents a singular noun. Therefore, a singular verb (contains) will be used with them. Hence, ‘contains’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Stanley ______ to play the violin now, with an amateur instructor.

solution.content: is learning ‘Is/am/are + V-ing’ is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence which is in the present continuous tense. Hence, ‘is learning(V-ing)’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Mohnish and Ravi _______ to Canada next month.

solution.content: are moving Present Continuous tense is used for events planned for the near future. Here, Mohnish and Ravi have planned to move to Canada next month. ‘Plural subject + are + V ing ’ is the correct grammatical structure for present continuous tense. Hence, ‘are moving’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Currently, Mittu and Bittu ________ hard to meet the project deadline.

solution.content: are working ‘Is/am/are + V-ing’ is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence which is in the present continuous tense. Also, according to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject(Mittu and Bittu) always takes a plural verb(are). Hence, ‘are working(V-ing)’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The teacher asked the students to _______ their ideas during the class discussion.

solution.content: bring up The phrasal verb ‘​bring up’ means to start to talk about a particular subject. The given sentence states that the teacher asked the students to present their ideas during the class discussion. Hence, ‘bring up’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The war _______ badly damaged the country’s infrastructure.

solution.content: has ‘Singular Subject(war) + has + V 3 ’ is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence which is in the present perfect tense. Hence, ‘has’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The teacher asked the students to _______ their essays before the deadline.

solution.content: hand in The phrasal verb ‘​hand in’ means to submit. The given sentence states that the teacher asked the students to submit their essays before the deadline. Hence, ‘hand in’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The small coffee shop at the end of the road is____________.

solution.content: mine When possessive is written separate from the noun, we use pronouns such as mine, his, hers, yours, etc. In the given sentence, the possessive is written separate from its noun (coffee shop). Hence, ‘mine’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Gautam ______ all the documents by the time his senior advocate reached the court.

solution.content: had examined If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V 3 ) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V 2 ). Hence, ‘had examined(V 3 )’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: She was so busy ______writing that when the maid came ______she didn’t hear her.

solution.content: in, in In the first blank, ‘in’ is used after ‘busy’ to indicate the activity in which someone is engaged. And in the second blank, ‘in’ has been used to show the presence of a maid inside a room or house. Hence, ‘in, in’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Hurry up ! There’s still ________ work left to do.

question.content: He gazed around the room ______ lay hidden a treasure chest.

question.content: Each one of the participants in the annual function ________ an applause.

question.content: The air quality is so bad ______it becomes difficult to breathe.

question.content: Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own ________ .

question.content: She was known for her _____ attention to detail, always making sure everything was perfectly organised and in its proper place.

question.content: The mother ________ the chips because they were soggy.

question.content: During the meeting, he went on a long and angry _______ about how the project was being mismanaged.

question.content: All praised him when he soared in the business world, but the same people ______ him when he failed in business.

solution.content: Criticised ‘Criticised’ means finding fault. The given sentence states that All praised him when he soared in the business world, but the same people criticised him when he failed in business. Hence, ‘criticised’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Augmented Reality (AR) continues to develop and become more _______ among a wide range of applications.

solution.content: pervasive ‘Pervasive’ means spreading widely throughout an area or group. The given sentence states that Augmented Reality (AR) continues to develop and become more pervasive among a wide range of applications. Hence, ‘pervasive’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A / An _________ fellow cannot become an ideal teacher.

solution.content: idle ‘Idle’ means being inactive, not engaged in work or activities. The given sentence states that a person who is lazy or inactive cannot become an ideal teacher. Hence, ‘idle’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Virtual worlds are recently new phenomena in that they _________ people to meet and socially interact with others in a variety of online environments.

question.content: Our breathing rate can change almost instantaneously in response to stress or __________ .

question.content: The issue of fairness, which remained, was for consideration at the hearing to _________ the scheme.

question.content: Ancient Indians were never this ___________ minded.

question.content: And to think after all these years you still have the __________ to say such things to me!

question.content: The show played to full houses for a five-night run and ended to ___________ applause on Saturday night.

question.content: Her ribs were _________ but no longer painful.

question.content: The ________ term "wasteland" is proposed to be replaced by the term "urban commons."

question.content: Some were very shaky and unstable, others were _________ , and a few were both!

question.content: A loud thud woke up everybody and nobody knew what all the _________ was about.

question.content: The greatest source of income in India is ___________ from agriculture and related industries.

question.content: As he walked past the chambers, Samir asked everyone to quiet_________.

question.content: Aunt Petunia was _________ a box of after-dinner mints.

question.content: In more civilized times even the most _________ enemies were treated with dignity.

question.content: She was trying to help that little boy in the grocery ________.

question.content: Different cells express different proteins depending on which promoters are either active or _________.

question.content: There was a general hesitation and _____ to ignore the problem .

question.content: At first the water_______ blue, then grey.

question.content: Ram placed her in one of the_____ leather chairs opposite his desk.

question.content: I dump the tray on the side and start ______ up the dishwasher.

question.content: _______ on the silver tray like a white snake, the wedding garland was as thick as my forearm.

question.content: David always kept his ______ open for anything that might put them at risk.

question.content: Howard tried to speak but all that came out was an ______ squeaky gargle. (4th Shift)

question.content: We can usefully distinguish four types of claims that have been traditionally made using the ________ "human nature". (4th Shift)

question.content: In the early autumn fierce fighting took place, the Serbians bearing a prominent part.

question.content: The machine can be _______ to deliver a certain number of coins. (4th Shift)

question.content: A group of Googlers get together regularly to___________ and decide which events will be celebrated with a doodle. (4th Shift)

question.content: Vishal is going to read the story _______.

question.content: The friends decided to play cards to ______ time while waiting for the cab.

question.content: Ram was praised for his________leadership.

question.content: This drama is extremely informative__________life in Roman times.

solution.content: about . ‘About’ means a little more or less than. The given sentence states that this drama is extremely informative about life in Roman times. Hence, ‘about’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Arun and his wife were ______ a baby boy after 18 years of their marriage.

solution.content: blessed with. ‘Blessed with’ means to have something that you feel is special or lucky. The given sentence states that Arun and his wife were blessed with a baby boy after 18 years of their marriage. Hence, ‘blessed with’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The company’s profits were low and they were forced to __________ staff.

solution.content: lay off. ‘Lay off’ means to discharge a worker temporarily or permanently because of economic conditions or shortage of work. The given sentence states that the company’s profits were low and they were forced to discharge the staff. Hence, ‘lay off’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We ensure that you will get a __________ chauffeur with the right car for your day.

solution.content: uniformed. ‘Uniformed’ means wearing a uniform. The given sentence states that we ensure that you will get a uniformed chauffeur with the right car for your day. Hence, ‘uniformed’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: She rubbed her hands over her arms, and then ___________ her purse, haded inside the convenience store.

solution.content: grabbing . ‘Grabbing’ means to try to get or catch somebody/something. The given sentence states that she rubbed her hands over her arms, and then grabbing her purse, haded inside the convenience store. Hence, ‘grabbing’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The judge directed the advocate general to _________ an enquiry on the case.

solution.content: hold . ‘Hold’ means the act or manner of having somebody/something in your hand. The given sentence states that the judge directed the advocate general to hold an enquiry on the case. Hence, ‘hold’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Brady straightened, the ________ baton in hand.

solution.content: wooden . ‘Wooden’ means made of wood. The given sentence states that Brady straightened, the wooden baton in hand. Hence, ‘wooden’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A faint mist ________ over the valley.

solution.content: hung . ‘Hung’ means to stay in the air in a way that is unpleasant or threatening. The given sentence states that a faint mist hung over the valley. Hence, ‘hung’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The ________ weapons which are easily available in the market are a big threat to the security of some nations.

solution.content: ‘Deadly’ means causing or likely to cause death. The given sentence states that the deadly weapons which are easily available in the market are a big threat to the security of some nations. Hence, ‘deadly’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This year, orange prices are forecast to grow, despite an expected increase in global _______ .

solution.content: ‘Production’ means the making or growing of something, especially in large quantities. The given sentence states that this year, orange prices are forecast to grow, despite an expected increase in global. Hence, ‘production’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The crowing witch released a _________cackle as she turned the boy into a beast.

solution.content: Loud . ‘Cackle’ means to laugh in a loud, harsh way. The given sentence states that the crowing witch released a loud cackle(laughed in a loud & harsh way) as she turned the boy into a beast. Hence, ‘loud’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Writing down instructions, steps and remembering them can make you look really efficient and ________. (4th Shift)

solution.content: ‘Diligent’ means having or showing care in one's work or duties. The given sentence states that writing down instructions, steps and remembering them can make you look really efficient and diligent. Hence, ‘diligent’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: She has_________ her money and jewellery to help the poor.

solution.content: ‘Given away’ is a phrase that means to donate or to give a gift/money to someone. The given sentence states that she has given away her money and jewellery to help the poor. Hence, ‘given away’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Kajol is one age’-defying beauty and her sari collection is worth _________.

solution.content: ‘Bookmarking’ means to mark or save something so that you can find it easily again. The given sentence states that Kajol is one age-defying beauty and her sari collection is worth bookmarking. Hence, ‘bookmarking’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A gaggle of journalists sit in a / an _________ foyer waiting impatiently.

solution.content: Hotel - an establishment providing accommodation, meals, and other services for travellers and tourists Attic - a space or room inside or partly inside the roof of a building Ranch - a large farm, especially in the western US and Canada, where cattle or other animals are bred and raised Croft - a very small farm around a house

question.content: I felt_________elated at the news. (4th Shift)

solution.content: ‘Strangely’ means in an unusual or surprising way. The given sentence states that the narrator felt strangely (surprisingly) elated at the news. Hence, ‘strangely’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: There was a ____________accident last night and the inspector on deputy was unable to raise help when she called from the mountains.

solution.content: ‘Serious’ means something severe in effect. The given sentence states that there was a serious accident last night and the inspector on deputy was unable to raise help when she called from the mountains. Hence, ‘serious’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: His heart pounded as he checked his rearview mirror and saw only the dark _______ of highway. (4th Shift)

solution.content: Stretch ‘Stretch’ means a continuous area or expanse of land. The given sentence states that the one who is talked about in the sentence saw the dark expanse of highway in his rear view mirror. Hence, ‘stretch’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: After a tiring day, the workers decided to_______ to restore their energy.

options.text: put a spoke in the wheel

solution.content: ‘ Hit the sack ’ is an idiom that means to go to bed. The given sentence states that after a tiring day, the workers decided to go to bed to restore their energy. Hence, ‘hit the sack’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: James Bernard was undoubtedly one of the greatest elocutionists of the world. Everyone agreed that he possessed the_________.

solution.content: gift of the gab ‘Gift of the gab’ is an idiom that means the ability to speak with eloquence and fluency. The given sentence states that James Bernard was undoubtedly one of the greatest elocutionists of the world. Everyone agreed that he possessed the ability to speak with eloquence. Hence, ‘gift of the gab’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: It is never advisable to have an axe to ________.

solution.content: ‘ An axe to grind ’ is an idiom that means to have a private reason for doing or being involved in something. The given sentence states that it is never advisable to have a private reason for doing something.

question.content: The annual meeting of our club has been ______ till next month.

solution.content: Deferred ‘Defer’ means to postpone. The given sentence states that the annual meeting of our club has been postponed till next month. Hence, ‘deferred’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The boy ______ to take the money.

solution.content: Refused ‘Refused’ means to say or show that you are not willing to accept something. The given sentence states that the boy refused(not willing) to take the money. question.content: The ______ of the knife in his hand made her sick.

solution.content: ‘Sight’ means to suddenly see something or someone. The given sentence states that suddenly seeing a knife in his hand made her sick. Hence, ‘sight’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The ______ needs of the inhabitants seem to be fruit, iced drinks, shiny boots and lottery tickets.

solution.content: ‘Principle’ means the most important thing. The given sentence states that the most important needs of the inhabitants seem to be fruit, iced drinks, shiny boots and lottery tickets. Hence, ‘principle’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: There are good points to each side and we need more ______ people that are willing to look at them from all angles.

solution.content: unbiased ‘Unbiased’ means fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something. The given sentence talks about some people who are not likely to support one side and are willing to look at each side from all angles. Hence, ‘unbiased’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: One of the children stood at the door to ______ if he saw the apparitor coming, who was an officer of the spiritual court.

solution.content: ‘ Give notice ’ is a phrase that means to inform or warn someone of something. The given sentence states that one of the children stood at the door to inform of the apparitor’s arrival. Hence, ‘give notice’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The boys were tired, but not too tired to examine the little hut ______

solution.content: ‘Thoroughly’ means in a careful and complete way. The given sentence talks about examining the little hut in a careful and complete way. Hence, ‘thoroughly’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Thus, ______ of their purpose, the three knights tried another plan.

solution.content: ‘Foiled’ means to prevent a plan from succeeding. The given sentence states that the three knights didn’t succeed in their purpose so they tried another plan. Hence, ‘foiled’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: In all cases, we have to ______ the facts from the various reports and documents.

solution.content: ‘Distil’ means to extract the essence of something. The given sentence states that in all cases, we have to extract the facts from the various reports and documents. Hence, ‘distil’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The ocean waves swelled and reached ______ her head, and she started screaming.

solution.content: ‘Above’ means higher than or overhead. The given sentence states that the ocean waves swelled and reached above her head, and she started screaming. Hence, ‘above’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: ______ your remaining project if you get groceries for me from the market.

solution.content: If two actions take place in the future then the 1st action must be in the present tense(V 1 ) and the 2nd action must be in the future tense(will/shall). Hence, ‘will do’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Writing books about how to ______ on the internet seems like a great idea.

solution.content: ‘ Make a fortune’ is a phrase that means to acquire great wealth by one's own efforts. The given sentence states that writing books about how to acquire great wealth by one's own efforts on the internet seems like a great idea. Hence, ‘make a fortune’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The Lebanese army raided the boat and ______ dozens of water bottles, tuna cans, loaves of bread, boxes of Picon cheese and life jackets.

solution.content: ‘Discovered’ means to find or learn something that nobody had found or knew before. The given sentence states that the Lebanese army raided the boat and discovered dozens of water bottles, tuna cans, etc. Hence, ‘discovered’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The US has become far more ______ to people with all kinds of food sensitivities and diet regimens.

solution.content: ‘Accommodating’ means agreeing to do or provide what somebody wants. The given sentence states that the US has become far more accommodating to people with all kinds of food sensitivities and diet regimens. Hence, ‘accommodating’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: All of my efforts to save her life have gone in ______.

solution.content: ‘Vain’ means failing to produce the result you want. The given sentence states that all of my efforts to save her life failed to produce results. Hence, ‘vain’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The garret where he lay at night had long been ______, and a great number of mice had made their home in it.

solution.content: ‘Vacant’ means not being used. The given sentence states that the garret where he lay at night had long been vacant, and a great number of mice had made their home in it. Hence, ‘vacant’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Ms. Gupta expressed her ______ for my political understanding.

solution.content: ‘Admiration’ means a feeling of liking and respecting somebody / something very much. The given sentence states that Ms. Gupta expressed her admiration for my political understanding. Hence, ‘admiration’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Danny lay on his back staring at  the ______ of his room.

solution.content: ‘Ceiling’ means the top surface of the inside of a room. The given sentence states that Danny lay on his back staring at the top surface of his room. Hence, ‘ceiling’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The girl ran into the house to get some ______ of bread, cold potatoes and other such morsels that were suitable for the fowls.

solution.content: ‘Crumbs’ means a very small dry piece of bread. The given sentence states that the girl ran into the house to get some crumbs of bread. Hence, ‘crumbs’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Sun Tzu says that ______ the enemy without battle requires greater skill than winning on the battlefield.

solution.content: ‘Defeating’ is a gerund that means to win a game, a fight, a vote, etc. against somebody. The given sentence states that Sun Tzu says that defeating the enemy without battle requires greater skill than winning on the battlefield. Hence, ‘defeating’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A person must speak eloquently and ______ while making a speech.

solution.content: ‘Politely’ means behaving in a way that shows good manners toward others. The given sentence states that a person must speak eloquently and politely while making a speech. Hence, ‘politely’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The sudden death of our uncle was ______________ for all of us.

solution.content: ‘Tragic’ means that makes you very sad, especially because it involves death. The given sentence states that the sudden death of our uncle was tragic for all of us. Hence, ‘tragic’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Thinking of talent as innate makes our world more manageable and more comfortable as it relieves a person of the _______ of expectation.

solution.content: ‘Burden’ means a responsibility or difficult task that causes a lot of work or worry. The given sentence states that thinking of talent as innate makes our world more manageable and more comfortable as it relieves a person of the burden of expectation. Hence, ‘burden’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: As he went through the street on an ______ that , he saw a woman with a cat under her arm. (Afternoon)

solution.content: ‘Errand’ means a short journey to take or get something for somebody. The given sentence states that as he went through the street on an errand that morning, he saw a woman with a cat under her arm. Hence, ‘errand’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The situation turned ugly as the crowd ______ to riot.

solution.content: The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in the simple past form(V 2 ). Hence, ‘began(V 2 )’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Many people may not find the rewards ______ with the time and effort required.

solution.content: ‘Commensurate’ means suitable in amount or quality compared to something else. The given sentence states that many people may not find the rewards commensurate with the time and effort required. Hence, ‘commensurate’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: If we don't reverse course now, will anyone take anything we say about justice and ___________ with any seriousness for decades to come?

solution.content: ‘Righteousness’ means the quality of being morally right or justifiable. The given sentence states that If we don't reverse course now, will anyone take anything we say about justice and righteousness with any seriousness for decades to come. Hence, ‘righteousness’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This cruise ship ______ in November and December.

solution.content: ‘Sails’ means to travel on water in a ship or boat. The given sentence states that this cruise ship sails in November and December. Hence, ‘sails’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Rescuers used a special device for finding people ______ in collapsed buildings.

solution.content: ‘Trapped’ means to catch and keep or store something. The given sentence states that rescuers used a special device for finding people trapped in collapsed buildings. Hence, ‘trapped’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: But if you ______ to spare before you do catch the bus, be sure to pop in.

solution.content: ‘ Have a moment ’ means have a short period of time available for something. The given sentence states that if you have a short period of time available to spare before you do catch the bus, be sure to pop in. Hence, ‘have a moment’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: John ran pretty fast, ______________ he did not win the race.

solution.content: ‘Though’ means in spite of the fact that. The given sentence states that John ran pretty fast, though he did not win the race. Hence, ‘though’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We ______ learn to meet adversity gracefully.

solution.content: ‘Must’ means used for saying that it is necessary that something happens. The given sentence states that we must learn to meet adversity gracefully. Hence, ‘must’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We deplore the use of ______ against innocent people.

solution.content: ‘Violence’ means behaviour which harms or damages somebody/something physically. The given sentence states that we deplore the use of violence against innocent people. Hence, ‘violence’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: India continues to ____________ the highest amount of e-waste, more than China, the US, Japan and Germany.

solution.content: ‘Generate’ means to produce or create something. The given sentence states that India continues to generate the highest amount of e-waste, more than China, the US, Japan and Germany. Hence, ‘generate’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The ______ of directors will decide the penalty.

solution.content: ‘Board’ means a group of people who control an organization, company, etc. The given sentence states that the board of directors will decide the penalty. Hence, ‘board’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The reality of the effects of rising aviation industry emissions on climate change has been known for decades, yet the industry and its emissions has continued to grow without _________.

solution.content: ‘Constraint’ means something that limits you. The given sentence states that the industry and its emissions has continued to grow without constraint. Hence, ‘constraint’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He didn't tell me anything ______ that he needed some money.

solution.content: ‘Except’ means not including somebody/something. The given sentence states that he didn't tell me anything except that he needed some money. Hence, ‘except’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The commander abjured his ______to the king.

solution.content: ‘Allegiance’ means support for a leader, government, belief, etc. The given sentence states that the commander abjured his allegiance to the king. Hence, ‘allegiance’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Mr. Pearson interrupted their harmless ______ and reminded them of the seriousness of the situation.

solution.content: ‘Chatter’ means to talk quickly or for a long time about something unimportant. The given sentence states that Mr. Pearson interrupted their harmless chatter and reminded them of the seriousness of the situation. Hence, ‘chatter’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: She refused to back ______, so she was fired from the company.

solution.content: ‘ Back down’ means to admit that you were wrong. The given sentence states that she refused to admit that she was wrong, so she was fired from the company. Hence, ‘down’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) ______ the idea of ‘tipping points’ two decades ago.

solution.content: ‘Introduced’ means to bring in something new for the first time. The given sentence states that the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) introduced the idea of ‘tipping points’ two decades ago. Hence, ‘introduced’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: She smashed a ______ of glass with the metal vase.

solution.content: ‘Pane’ means a piece of glass in a window, etc. The given sentence states that she smashed a pane of glass with the metal vase. Hence, ‘pane’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I organised my dressing table by putting all the rubber bands ______ the drawer.

solution.content: The preposition ‘in’ means inside or to a position inside a particular area or object. The given sentence states that I organised my dressing table by putting all the rubber bands in the drawer. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Most mainliners do not view modern culture as inherently ______ to religious belief.

solution.content: ‘Inimical’ means harmful to something. The given sentence states that most mainliners do not view modern culture as inherently inimical to religious belief. Hence, ‘inimical’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: ______ I learned that there was a gift for each child, I was delighted.

solution.content: ‘When’ is used for talking about the time at which something happens. The given sentence states that when I learned that there was a gift for each child, I was delighted. Hence, ‘When’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I feel so lazy and ______ after doing any strenuous work.

solution.content: ‘Sluggish’ means moving or working more slowly than normal in a way that seems lazy. The given sentence states that I feel so lazy and sluggish after doing any strenuous work. Hence, ‘sluggish’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: My mother is a ____ and forgiving person.

solution.content: ‘Compassionate’ means feeling or showing sympathy and sadness for the suffering of others. The given sentence states that my mother is a compassionate and forgiving person. Hence, ‘compassionate’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The court has absolved him ______ all the charges levied against him.

solution.content: We generally use the preposition ‘of’ with the verb ‘absolved’ . The given sentence states that the court has absolved him of all the charges levied against him. Hence, ‘of’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Smoking is ______ in my office building.

solution.content: ‘Banned’ means to officially say that something is not allowed, often by law. The given sentence states that smoking is not allowed in my office building. Hence, ‘banned’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The skill of execution is viewed as inseparable from art, and mastery of technical problems is a ______ for producing expressive interpretations.

solution.content: ‘Precondition’ means something that must happen or exist before something else can exist. The given sentence states that the skill of execution is viewed as inseparable from art, and mastery of technical problems is a precondition for producing expressive interpretations. Hence, ‘precondition’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I can’t fit this teddy bear in my almirah. It is so ______.

solution.content: ‘Gigantic’ means extremely big. The given sentence states that I can’t fit this teddy bear in my almirah. It is so gigantic. Hence, ‘gigantic’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The bank was prepared to ______ chance and lend him 40% of the purchase price.

solution.content: ‘ Take a chance’ is a phrase that means to put one's trust in something or someone knowing that it may not be safe or certain. The given sentence states that the bank was prepared to take a chance and lend him 40% of the purchase price. Hence, ‘take a’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The Armenian language has many dialects, some of which cannot be ______ by speakers of other dialects.

solution.content: ‘Understood’ means to know or realize the meaning of something. The given sentence states that the Armenian language has many dialects, some of which cannot be understood by speakers of other dialects. Hence, ‘understood’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The RTE Act bears many similarities to the US's No Child Left Behind Act, ______school accountability, assessment standards and teacher training.

solution.content: ‘Including’ means having as a part. The given sentence states that the RTE Act bears many similarities to the US's No Child Left Behind Act, including school accountability, assessment standards and teacher training. Hence, ‘including’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Several pictures and videos have been circulating ______ social media featuring her.

solution.content: The given sentence states that several pictures and videos have been circulating on social media featuring her. Hence, ‘ on ’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Only 30 percent worked in companies where paternity leave was an_____.

solution.content: ‘Entitlement’ means the official right to have or do something. The given sentence states that only 30 percent worked in companies where paternity leave was an entitlement. Hence, ‘entitlement’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: A nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously held that Indians have a / an_____protected fundamental right to privacy.

solution.content: ‘Constitutionally’ means in a way that is in accordance with a political constitution. The given sentence states that a nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously held that Indians have a constitutionally protected fundamental right to privacy. Hence, ‘constitutionally’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The mystery behind the extinction of the dinosaurs______obscure.

solution.content: ‘Still’ means continuing until now or until the time you are talking about and not finishing. The given sentence states that the mystery behind the extinction of the dinosaurs is still obscure. Hence, ‘is still’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The lottery is a regular weekly_______where the drawing of the numbers is done by a little girl.

solution.content: ‘Recreation’ means enjoying yourself and relaxing when you are not working. The given sentence states that the lottery is a regular weekly recreation where the drawing of the numbers is done by a little girl. Hence, ‘recreation’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Anita looked______the word in the dictionary, but she still did not understand it.

solution.content: ‘ Look up ’ means to check a fact or get information about something. The given sentence states that Anita looked up the word in the dictionary, but she still did not understand it. Hence, ‘up’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: We need to____ for next week, so are you in or out?

solution.content: ‘Plan’ means a detailed scheme, method, etc, for attaining an objective. The given sentence states that we need to make plans for next week, so are you in or out. Hence, ‘make plans’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: This small hut is going to be my____for the next three days.

solution.content: ‘Abode’ means the place where you live. The given sentence states that this small hut is going to be my abode for the next three days. Hence, ‘abode’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: He believed that he had struck terror in his children's hearts because of his_______.

solution.content: ‘Rage’ means a feeling of violent anger that is difficult to control. The given sentence states that he believed that he had struck terror in his children's hearts because of his rage. Hence, ‘rage’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: It was raining heavily, that's why your father____at my place last night.

solution.content: ‘Stayed’ means to continue to be somewhere and not go away. The given sentence states that it was raining heavily, that's why your father stayed at my place last night. Hence, ‘stayed’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: The weather was so____that she couldn't step out of the house.

solution.content: ‘Terrible’ means very unpleasant, causing great shock or injury. The given sentence states that the weather was so terrible that she couldn't step out of the house. Hence, ‘terrible’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Food was_____; guides were not to be found, and the enemy dogged them all the way.

solution.content: ‘Scarce’ means insufficient to satisfy the need or demand. The given sentence states that food was scarce; guides were not to be found, and the enemy dogged them all the way. Hence, ‘scarce’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: It was a long and dangerous journey in those unsettled days. The pilgrim had to face______by land and sea.

solution.content: ‘Peril’ means something that is very dangerous. The given sentence states that the pilgrim had to face perils by land and sea. Hence, ‘perils’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Farmers are urged to ______ to good agricultural practices in the disposal and spreading of agricultural wastes such as slurry.

solution.content: ‘Adhere’ means to stick firmly to something. The given sentence states that farmers are urged to adhere to good agricultural practices in the disposal and spreading of agricultural wastes such as slurry. Hence, ‘adhere’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: I __________ walked down the stairs, careful to be as quiet as possible.

solution.content: ‘Cautiously’ means be very careful about what you do or say. The given sentence states that I cautiously walked down the stairs, careful to be as quiet as possible. Hence, ‘cautiously’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: Most natural diamonds have some type of______.

solution.content: ‘Flaw’ means a mistake in something that makes it not good enough. The given sentence states that most natural diamonds have some type of flaw. Hence, ‘flaw’ is the most appropriate answer.

question.content: When we believe that our mind is thinking ______ thoughts at the same time, what actually is happening is that __________ thoughts are __________ in such quick ___________ so as to seem simultaneous

solution.content: We will use the words ‘multiple’ & ‘myriad’ in the given sentence because they are generally used before a plural noun(thoughts). However, all the remaining words given in option c perfectly fit in the context of the given sentence.

question.content: My grandfather was a farmer and he ___________three acres of land.
